about: Proposed unit, category, land kind and need of each existing resource (D1, D3). Proposals, to be confirmed; catalogue.py joins them to the facts from the XML. Roles (D16): every system the statement names in which a good takes part, with the existing buildings and units it touches; "need" is the need role only, kept for catalogue.py.

roles.what: Meat (beef): dietary variety
Oxen as draught animals for ploughs and carts, with leather harness
Breeding stock: the herd that yields dairy, leather and meat (D15, LQ.F11)
Meat (mutton): dietary variety
Breeding stock: the flock that yields wool, dairy, leather and meat (D15, LQ.F11)

BONUS_WOOL.note: Yielded by sheep pastures (D10, LQ.F11); nothing placed, gave or used it before.

roles.what: Clothing for warmth: the clothing need of every citizen (D13), larger with size and era
Cloth and felt: the textile trade's raw material, from household spinning to the cloth guilds and textile mills
Tents, blankets, padding under armour, uniforms, and sails in the northern tradition
Durable once shorn and cleaned
Shipped in bales; a principal trade good of the ancient and medieval economies
Sheep, the breeding stock (D15)

BONUS_CGUILDPAPER.note: From the Guilds module; nothing places, gives or uses it in the base records.

BONUS_HORSE.note: "head": live animals; the one unit outside tonnes, bales, barrels and crates.

roles.what: Draught, transport and mounts, with leather harness and saddles
Breeding stock: horses and leather (LQ.F11)

BONUS_BERNSTEIN.note: Amber; yielded by cottages, hamlets and villages today.

BONUS_DRAMA.note: Not a physical good: given by buildings (theatre culture). Proposed to stay a building-given resource outside the goods accounts (open question Q2).

BONUS_MUSIC.note: Not a physical good: given by buildings. Proposed to stay a building-given resource outside the goods accounts (Q2).

BONUS_MOVIES.note: Not a physical good: given by buildings. Proposed to stay a building-given resource outside the goods accounts (Q2).

BONUS_ANCIENTTEMPLE.note: A site, not a good: an explorable ruin with its own improvement. Proposed to stay a plot feature of the map (Q2).

BONUS_THERMAL_VENT.note: A site, not a good: no improvement yields or trades it. Proposed to stay a plot feature of the map (Q2).

BONUS_TIMBER.note: New (R1): lumber camps and lumbermills on forest; also the fuel before coal (D12) and a building material.

roles.what: Firewood for heating and cooking: the fuel need of every settlement from the start (D12), larger with size; coal and then oil take over the need in their eras
Charcoal for workshops before coal: smelting and smithing, glass, brewing, kilns

The building material of everything built before steel and concrete: houses, walls, granaries, markets, harbours and the scaffolding of stone buildings; then pit props for mines and sleepers for railways
where: buildings of the ancient to medieval eras

roles.what: Hulls and masts of every wooden ship; carts and wagons of settlers and workers; tools' handles; bows, shafts and siege engines
Durable and bulky: keeps, but storage space limits stocks
Shipped in tonnes; forest-poor regions import it
None: timber comes from forest land (LQ.F10); the means is the forest itself

BONUS_DAIRY.note: New (R1): co-product of cow and sheep pastures.

roles.what: Dietary variety: milk, cheese and butter; part of the variety need with meat, fish, fruit and oil (statement 3.3); feeds growth and health, larger with size
where: the market chain (Market, Fair, Commodity Market, Commercial Center)

Cheese as rations for armies in the field and ships' provisions
Shipped in tonnes; fresh dairy only to near partners, cheese and canned dairy far
Dairy cattle and sheep, the breeding stock (D15)

BONUS_LEATHER.note: New (R1): co-product of horse, cow and sheep pastures.

roles.what: Clothing: footwear, belts and coats; part of the clothing need (D13)
Tools and equipment of production: harness and yokes that put draught animals to ploughs, carts and mills; bellows of forges; buckets, waterskins, straps; drive belts of early machinery

roles.what: Parchment and bookbinding: the writing material before paper
Saddles and harness of mounted units and chariots; shields, jerkins and bracers of early infantry and archers
Durable once tanned

Cattle, horses, sheep and pigs, the breeding stock (D15)

role_kinds.need: consumed per citizen to meet a need (statement 3.3); effects of supply and of shortfall; component CN
role_kinds.material: used up to make something: buildings, units, tools, other goods (3.2, 3.5); components PR.F3, IN.F1, IN.F2
role_kinds.fuel: burnt for heat in homes and in workshops (3.3 fuel need; 3.5 recipes); components CN, IN.F1
role_kinds.storage: how the good keeps: perishable or durable, and what preserves it (3.1, 3.4); components SD.F1, SD.F2, FG.F2
role_kinds.supplies: drawn by units in the field (3.5); component IN.F3
role_kinds.trade: shipped in deals as a quantity (4.1); component TR.F2
role_kinds.means: the stock or seed that lets the buyer produce a good (4.1); component TR.F3

production.about: Proposal for PR.F1 (R10, M53): a worked tile's output from the real people employed on it, the technologies and resources available, land quality and the kind of good. Status: open (D23). Figures marked 'source' come from the sources listed; figures marked 'estimate' are mine, to be replaced by sourced ones.

model.formula: output per year (tonnes) = area worked (ha) x gross yield (t/ha) x land quality x (1 - seed share)
model.area_worked: min(the tile's arable area, workers on the tile x hectares one worker can farm at the owner's technology)
model.workers: the real people one working citizen stands for (open: D23 question 2)
model.yield: per good and technology stage; the game's own farm techs (IMPROVEMENT_FARM TechYieldChanges) are the stages
model.land_quality: a multiplier per tile and good: today from terrain, fresh water and the placed resource; land qualities (LD) replace it later
model.integers: whole tonnes per year; a size-20 city of 4.4 million at about 0.25 t of grain each eats about 1.1 million t a year, far below 2^31 (rule F)

game_facts.real_population: CvCity::getRealPopulation = size^2.8 x 1000: size 1 = 1,000; size 8 = 337,000; size 20 = 4.4 million (per citizen: 1,000; 42,000; 220,000)
game_facts.turn_length_normal: GAMESPEED_NORMAL (CIV4GameSpeedInfo.xml): 50 years a turn for 40 turns, 25 for 100, 20 for 120, 10 for 50, 5 for 80, 2 for 80, 1 for 60, half a year for 150, a quarter for 20: 700 turns
game_facts.farm_techs: IMPROVEMENT_FARM: +2 food irrigated; +1 food each at Fermentation, Mathematics, Waterworks, Crop Rotation, Biology, Pesticides, Machine Tools (-1 production), Gene Manipulation

stages.basis: source: Winchester manors c.1300 gross 0.515 t/ha, net 0.385, 4 grains per grain sown (Pretty 1990); Columella 42 person-days/ha before harvest (White 1965), 78 with missing tasks (Rosenstein): 250 working days give 3-6 ha
estimate: Roman estate management; Kent manors before 1303 about 0.8 t/ha at 2.9 grains per grain (Mate 1985, my conversion)
estimate: four-course rotation with clover; to be sourced (English yields about 1800)
source: UK wheat just over 2 t/ha in the early 20th century (Mackay et al. 2020, PMC7211843); US wheat 56 worker-hours per acre in 1800
estimate for yield; source for labour: US wheat 3 worker-hours per acre by 1970 (about 7 h/ha)
source: UK wheat about 8 t/ha today (Mackay et al. 2020)

wheat.not_mapped: Fermentation and Waterworks also raise the farm's food in the game; proposed: Waterworks raises land quality on watered land (irrigation), Fermentation changes no wheat yield (it belongs to drink, IN)
wheat.example: Before Mathematics, 17,000 workers on a good wheat tile (if a size-8 city's working citizen stands for 40 % of its 42,000 people): 17,000 x 3 ha x 0.5 t x 1.0 x 0.75 = 19,125 t a year; the city's 337,000 people at about 0.2 t of grain each eat about 67,000 t, so about three such tiles with other foods

land_quality_today.basis: estimate; rich = flood plains or a river with the crop's resource, good = grassland or plains with the resource or fresh water, poor = otherwise; the best single Winchester harvest (1.8 t/ha against 0.5) shows the spread is real

production.other_goods: The same model per good: rice (higher yield, more labour per ha), corn, potato (fresh weight), livestock (head and product per head per year: milk, wool, hides), timber (cubic metres or tonnes per woodcutter per year), ore (tonnes per miner per year). Written after D23 is decided, each with sources.
sources: Pretty, J. (1990) Sustainable Agriculture in the Middle Ages: The English Manor, Agricultural History Review 38: https://www.bahs.org.uk/AGHR/ARTICLES/38n1a1.pdf
Mate, M. (1985) Medieval Agrarian Practices: The Determining Factors?, Agricultural History Review 33: https://www.bahs.org.uk/AGHR/ARTICLES/33n1a2.pdf
Columella, De Re Rustica II.12 (via secondary summaries; White 1965, Spurr, Rosenstein): https://acoup.blog/2025/09/05/collections-life-work-death-and-the-peasant-part-ivb-working-days/
Mackay, I. et al. (2020) estimating the upper yield boundary of winter wheat: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7211843/
US worker-hours per acre of wheat 1800-1970 (teaching resource): https://www.digitalhistory.uh.edu/disp_textbook.cfm?psid=3837&smtID=11
